step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram shows the data architecture of Jubilant Foodworks (Domino's/Dunkin' Donuts master franchisee in South Asia). Point of Sale (POS) systems and E-Commerce applications feed data into databases (POS DB and MySQL DB). DMS migrates data from the E-COMM database into an S3 data lake raw layer, while ETL scripts load POS database data to S3. EMR jobs process data in S3 (curating layers) and load hot data into Redshift. Redshift Spectrum transparently queries cold/warm data residing in S3. Athena executes ad-hoc SQL queries directly on S3 data to provide business insights.

graph.notes: Architecture handles ~200,000 orders/day across ~1,250 restaurants, hitting up to 1,500 orders per minute at peak.

edges.notes: E-commerce orders flow into POS machines for restaurant fulfillment.
E-commerce transactions stored in MySQL DB.
POS machine data flows into consolidation POS DB.
DMS reads transaction data from MySQL DB.
DMS loads data into S3 raw layer.
Custom ETL scripts transform and load POS DB data to S3 raw layer.
EMR reads raw data from S3 for processing.
EMR writes back processed/curated data to S3 curated layer.
EMR loads hot data (last 5-6 months) into Redshift.
Redshift Spectrum transparently queries warm/cold data in S3 data lake.
Athena queries historical data stored in S3 data lake.
S3 returns query result data back to Athena.
